title: security-compliance-review-prep-1on1-priya-desai-2026-03
content:
Purpose:
Quick prep notes for 1:1 with Alex (Head of Security) — align on SOC2/ISO readiness, vendor risk items flagged in Q1, and near-term audit evidence needs. Goal is to leave with a prioritized list of action owners and dates.

Context / current state summary:
- SOC2: In progress. Core controls mapped; evidence gaps remain for change management (CM-3) and access review cadence (AC-2). Controls owner list updated in Confluence, but a few repos missing owners.
- ISO27001: Scope draft approved for infra and platform services; gap analysis completed – remediation estimates in progress.
- Vendor risk: 12 vendors in critical tier; 3 vendors (log-storage, ML feature store, infra-monitoring) have outstanding questionnaires or expired AOCs.
- Audit readiness: Target window Q2 (tentative). Need finalized evidence packet and runbook for auditor access.

Agenda (30 min):
1) Quick sync on SOC2 control status (5 min)
   - highlight CM-3, AC-2 gaps (owners: Eng-Platform / SRE)
2) Vendor risk hotlist (8 min)
   - confirm plan for log-storage, feature-store, infra-monitoring vendors
3) Evidence collection & access runbook (7 min)
   - who will assemble artifacts, where to store, who gets auditor access?
4) Prioritization & owners (6 min)
   - agree owners, deadlines, blockers
5) Next steps / follow-ups (4 min)

Key questions I want to raise:
- Do we lock Q2 as the audit window now or wait for vendor remediations? Pros/cons?
- For CM-3 (change management): is the current ticket tagging + PR policy sufficient as evidence or do auditors expect a separate change log export?
- For access reviews (AC-2): can we commit to quarterly reviews starting Apr 2026? Who signs off?
- Vendor AOCs: can we accept recent SOC2 reports for the log-storage vendor, or do we need a fresh AOC?

Notes / talking points:
- CM-3: We have automated approvals for infra repos but not for some legacy service repos. Proposed: 2-week sprint to add PR template + required checks; need SRE + infra eng bandwidth.
- AC-2: Currently ad-hoc access reviews. Recommend automated weekly export to HR/Identity for review and quarterly attestation by team leads.
- Evidence locations: create a dedicated Confluence space plus a Read-only S3 bucket (bucket: s3://redwood-audit-evidence-q2-2026) with time-limited presigned URLs for auditors.
- Vendor follow-up: Ops to ping vendor contacts this week; if AOC not received in 10 business days escalate to procurement.

Immediate action items (owner / due):
- Priya: Draft evidence collection checklist and Confluence page structure (due 2026-03-06)
- Maya Thompson: Reach out to log-storage vendor for AOC status and confirm latest report (due 2026-03-09)
- Sam Lee: Assess legacy repos missing CM automation and produce a short remediation plan + estimate (due 2026-03-11)
- Alex (Head of Security): Approve quarterly access review cadence and sign off on runbook (target 2026-03-10)
- Procurement: Place vendor escalation for infra-monitoring if no AOC in 10 business days (owner: procurement@redwood.com, due by 2026-03-12)

Risks / blockers to highlight:
- Hiring/engineering bandwidth for CM automation — may push evidence readiness beyond audit window.
- Some vendors are slow to respond; may require contract-level enforcement.
- Potential scope creep for ISO if app-level services added; need to lock scope by end of March.

Follow-up / next meeting:
- Schedule 30-min checklist review with Eng-Platform and SRE (invite: Maya, Sam, Alex) — target week of 2026-03-15.
- Capture outcomes in Confluence and update the Jira tickets (SEC-3421 for SOC2 evidence tracker).

Notes to self:
- Bring sample evidence export (access logs, PR change log example) to 1:1 in case Alex asks for concrete examples.
- Save vendor contact emails into the linked artifacts list after the meeting.

Version / provenance:
- Draft v0.2 — working notes. Will convert to official prep doc in Confluence once owners/ dates confirmed.
